title: 没(有): didn't, haven't
summary: Lets you say something did not happen, using 没 or 没有 before the verb and dropping 了, as in 我没去.
structure: Subject + 还没(有) + Verb (+ 呢)
explanation:
不 and 没 both mean 'not', but they do different jobs. 没 (or 没有) says an action did NOT happen: 我昨天没去 'I didn't go yesterday.' 不 is for habits, wishes and the future: 我不去 'I'm not going / I don't go.'

When you use 没, drop the 了 that a finished action would have: 我吃了 → 我没吃. 没 and 没有 mean the same before a verb; 没 is shorter and more common in speech.

examples.en: I didn't go to school yesterday.

mistakes.why: For something that didn't happen in the past, use 没, not 不.

exercises.en: I didn't buy a phone yesterday.
why: 不 is for habits and the future, not a past event.
Never add 了 to 没 like this.
Correct: a habit is negated with 不.
没 would mean 'I didn't drink tea (that time)'.
没有 also means 'didn't'; for a habit use 不.
Correct: 没 + verb, and 了 goes.
不 doesn't negate a finished action, and 了 must go.
不来了 means 'isn't coming any more'.

exercises.en: My dad didn't go to work yesterday.
exercises.why: 没 goes straight before the verb.

exercises.prompt: Your friend asks 你吃饭了吗？ You haven't eaten. You say:
why: 不吃了 means 'I won't eat any more'.
Don't add 了 after 没.
